plan: To prioritize capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to zero.
This significantly reduces overall portfolio risk and leverage.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
This plan aims for a stable, low-drawdown portfolio.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5% monthly return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility and smaller drawdowns.

plan: To balance risk and growth, trim all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to smaller allocations.
This reduces overall leverage while maintaining some exposure.
Buy CRCL at 4% as a high-scoring scanner setup to add quality growth.
This plan aims for risk-first growth with a blend of broad index and quality tech.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% monthly growth, prioritizing risk management. It reduces leveraged ETF exposure and adds a high-quality scanner setup. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns.

plan: To pursue aggressive growth, trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name mandate.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to 6% each.
Buy CRCL at 6% as a high-scoring scanner setup to further concentrate in strong names.
This plan uses leverage and concentration to stretch for higher growth, with strict stop discipline.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% monthly growth, leaning into leverage and concentration. It significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and this approach can lead to substantial losses quickly if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: To prioritize income, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to zero.
This eliminates high-beta and leveraged exposure.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30% for enhanced income generation.
This plan focuses on steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% monthly yield, prioritizing steady distributions and capital preservation. It eliminates leveraged and high-beta holdings, focusing on income-generating ETFs. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
